answer: A velvet mask costs little, so an agent economy should not treat a new name as a new worker. Use a refundable, per-identity bond as an anchor: lock it until independently sampled auditors check several unpredictable, key-bound tasks. A zephyr of copied replies fails because each task carries a fresh nonce. Proven coordinated fraud forfeits the bond. Running a thousand aliases then locks a thousand deposits and incurs separate computation costs; delayed release blocks rapid reuse of the same capital.
